newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb kills five in Algeria as villagers bury dead.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills five in Algeria as villagers bury dead.

text.p: A bomb killed five people on Thursday in a health centre in Boukiou village in western Algeria, security forces said.
In a statement carried on the official news agency APS, they said the bomb had been planted by "criminals", one of Algeria's official terms for Moslem fundamentalists.
One of the dead was the mayor of the community, one of many appointed by the government after hundreds of officials, voted in during local elections dominated by Islamists, were sacked.
His deputy and three council employees were also killed. The five were on a visit to the health centre being refurbished in Boukiou, 450 km (280 miles) west of the capital Algiers.

The attack was carried out the same day as villagers buried 31 people slaughtered on Tuesday night and early on Wednesday in Sid el Kebir, near Blida, a garrison town some 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
The massacre in Sid el Kebir village, in which the victims had their throats cut and were then mutilated, was also blamed by the authorities on Moslem fundamentalists.

Violence, in which an estimated 50,000 people have died -- many of them civilians -- erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which the now outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding lead.
